newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Newspaper banned in Zaire over Mobutu report.
newsitem.headline: Newspaper banned in Zaire over Mobutu report.

text.p: Zaire's government banned a leading opposition newspaper on Wednesday after it published a report saying that President Mobutu Sese Seko would have an operation for throat cancer, officials said.
The owner and publisher of the newspaper, Le Palmares, had been detained and would stand trial for spreading false rumours, they added. The charge carries a sentence of one to 12 months in jail.
Information Minister Boguo Makeli signed the order suspending Le Palmares for an indefinite period. Officials said Monday's article had slighted the president.
"These false rumours were liable to alarm and worry the people," one said.
Mobutu's spokesman told Reuters the president, who had a prostate operation in Switzerland on August 22, was recovering well.
"We expect him to return home in three weeks," he added. "He needs rest but to this day there is no cause for concern about him."

Le Palmares publisher, Michel Luya, was arrested at his home on Tuesday. He has pleaded not guilty. He wrote the article that quoted a source living in the Swiss town of Lausanne as saying Mobutu was riddled with cancer.
Le Palmares was suspended for three months in 1993 after publishing a cartoon showing Mobutu weeping huge tears before the coffin of Belgian King Baudouin I. Belgium is the former colonial power.

Mobutu seized power in the vast Central African country in 1965. He ruled virtually unchallenged until 1990 when opposition protests and pressure from Zaire's foreign partners forced him along the path of democratic reform.
